title: Q5 v3: orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py + `scorecard --planner-routing` — Planner outcomes by model × decision type × band × class × architectural, non-inferiority evidence per class, economics (P7, P13, P16)
spec:
Why: no code joins Planner invocations to downstream engineering outcomes; premium_summary (planner_runs.py:843) counts launches and tokens only. The router (planner_router.py, T-0700) needs class_evidence and the brief (P7/P13/P16) a Planner scorecard with cold-start priors and a CLI. Spec review T-0683's risks are folded in: the producer is named and a dependency (planner_telemetry.py, T-0708), min_samples has an explicit source, the CRITERIA mapping is literal, the telemetry import is guarded, and this task is READ-SIDE: the scorecard stays empty in production until Wave B wires planner_runs to emit invocation rows (stated so reviewers do not expect a populated card after this merge).
What: new module orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py plus cli.py flag `scorecard --planner-routing [--json]`.
- Inputs: invocation rows via planner_telemetry.read_invocations_with_malformed(root) (rows merged by launch_id with fields launch_id, goal_id, kind, payload_keys, decision_type, model, tier, band, task_class, architectural, started_at, material, reescalation, total_tokens, usd, latency_s, outcome), bus tasks from root/tasks/*.json, spec_review and review tasks among them. Wrap `from . import planner_telemetry` in try/except ImportError so a missing module degrades to an empty card with card["error"] = "planner_telemetry unavailable". Malformed lines counted in card["malformed"].
- min_samples: explicit parameter wins; else cfg planner.routing.min_samples when int (the [planner.routing] table lands with this goal's pool.toml task and may be absent); else cfg promotion.min_samples; else 20.
- Attribution window: an invocation owns the goal's execute tasks whose lineage root (attribution.lineage(task)["root"]) has created_at >= invocation started_at and < the next invocation's started_at for the same goal (or +inf); fix rounds belong to their root's owner. A kind held invocation additionally owns the fix-round task whose constraints.fix_round_for equals that invocation's held task id (payload_keys[0] split at ':').
- group_key(row) -> f"{model}|{decision_type}|{band}|{task_class}|{'arch' if architectural else 'plain'}".
- build(root=STATE, *, cfg=None, min_samples=None) -> {"groups": {key: metrics}, "n", "malformed", "min_samples", "read_side_only": True}; metrics per group: n, material_rate, downstream_accepted_rate (owned roots with merged_into), first_pass_rate (owned roots with pipeline.lineage_fix_rounds in (0, None) and no fix-round children), fix_round_rate, avg_fix_rounds, gate_red_rate (pipeline.gate_reds > 0), review_request_changes_rate (review tasks whose inputs[0] is an owned id, verdict from review_verdict or result.verdict == request_changes), spec_review_approval_rate (same for spec_review role, verdict approve), replanning_rate (a later invocation of the same goal with decision_type architectural_replan), reescalation_rate (rows reescalation True), human_intervention_rate (None unless planner_telemetry.interactive_by_goal returns a row for the goal with a day after started_at; wrap the call in try/except Exception -> None), tokens_mean, usd_mean, latency_mean, evidence "sufficient"|"insufficient" (n >= min_samples).
- CRITERIA_MAP = {"first_pass_rate": ("first_pass_delta", ">=", -0.02), "avg_fix_rounds": ("fix_rounds_delta", "<=", 0.05), "gate_success": ("gate_success_delta", ">=", -0.02), "review_request_changes_rate": ("review_findings_delta", "<=", 0.10)}; thresholds read from promotion.CRITERIA by those keys, overridable via cfg["promotion"]; REESCALATION_MAX = 0.2 is this module's own constant. gate_success = 1 - gate_red_rate.
- class_evidence(model, decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, *, root=STATE, cfg=None, min_samples=None) -> {"n", "noninferior": True|False|None, "deltas": {metric: candidate - baseline}, "failed": [metric names], "reescalation_rate", "baseline_model"}: baseline group = same class with model == cfg [models].planner (fallback: rows with tier fable). None when either group has n < min_samples; False when any CRITERIA_MAP comparison fails or reescalation_rate > REESCALATION_MAX (failed lists "reescalation"); True otherwise. Tokens, usd, latency never enter the verdict (docstring + test).
- economics(root=STATE) -> per model {"planner_usd_per_accepted_goal", "planner_tokens_per_accepted_goal", "pipeline_usd_after_planning" (mean over invocations of the sum of scorecard.by_task usd for owned tasks), "expected_total_cost_after_planning": {decision_type: mean(planner usd + pipeline usd)}}; accepted goals via scorecard.accepted_goals(root).
- format(card) -> text table sorted by key with a first line 'read-side only: rows appear once planner_runs emits invocations' when n == 0; format_evidence(evidence) one line. cli.py: `sc.add_argument("--planner-routing", action="store_true")`, dispatch to build/format (json with --json), ap.error when combined with --planner or --parallelism (same style as the existing pair).
acceptance: tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_groups_by_model_type_band_class_arch — rows written with planner_telemetry.record_launch/record_usage/record_materiality under a sandbox root for two models and two decision types produce four group keys with n, material_rate and downstream_accepted_rate from owned tasks in the attribution window

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_attribution_window_and_fix_rounds_follow_root — a root task created after invocation A and its fix round created after invocation B both count toward A; a held-kind invocation owns the fix round with constraints.fix_round_for

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_class_evidence_noninferior_equivalent_worse_and_insufficient — opus equal to fable gives noninferior True; opus with first_pass_rate 0.3 lower gives False with failed naming first_pass_rate; n below min_samples gives None; a group with 1e9 tokens and 0 usd changes no verdict
tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_reescalation_penalises_class — reescalation_rate 0.5 on an otherwise equal class gives noninferior False with failed containing reescalation

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_cli_flag_min_samples_source_and_malformed_tolerance — `scorecard --planner-routing --json` under a sandbox root prints a card with read_side_only True, groups and malformed 1 for a runs dir containing one malformed line; min_samples comes from [planner.routing] when present, else [promotion], else 20; a patched ImportError for planner_telemetry yields card error text instead of a crash

constraints.interface_contract: Reads planner_telemetry.read_invocations_with_malformed(root) rows (T-0708). group_key(row) -> 'model|decision_type|band|task_class|arch|plain'. build(root, *, cfg, min_samples) -> {groups, n, malformed, min_samples, read_side_only}. class_evidence(model, decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, *, root, cfg, min_samples) -> {n, noninferior: True|False|None, deltas, failed, reescalation_rate, baseline_model} consumed by planner_router.decide(evidence=...). CRITERIA_MAP literal maps metrics to promotion.CRITERIA keys; REESCALATION_MAX 0.2. economics(root). CLI scorecard --planner-routing [--json]. Read-side only until Wave B emits rows from planner_runs.

result.summary: superseded by Q5 v4 after spec review request_changes (review_request_changes threshold is the module's own constant REVIEW_CHANGES_MAX_DELTA 0.10 rather than promotion's negative review_findings_delta; first_pass_rate and fix_round_rate only count owned roots in a terminal state: merged_into set, status failed, or pipeline.first_green_at present)

spec_review_risks.issue: CRITERIA_MAP maps review_request_changes_rate to ("review_findings_delta", "<=", 0.10), but promotion.py's actual CRITERIA["review_findings_delta"] default is -0.10 (orchestrator/promotion.py:30), and the spec says thresholds are 'read from promotion.CRITERIA by those keys' at runtime, not the illustrative literal. With comparator <= and the real value -0.10, an identical candidate/baseline pair (delta=0) evaluates 0 <= -0.10 -> False -> flagged as a regression on every comparison, which directly contradicts acceptance test test_class_evidence_noninferior_equivalent_worse_and_insufficient ('opus equal to fable gives noninferior True'). The other three CRITERIA_MAP entries (first_pass_rate, avg_fix_rounds, gate_success) have comparator direction and literal that agree with promotion.py's own bad()-check sign; only this fourth entry is inverted. This is also a hidden coupling risk independent of the sign bug: reusing promotion.py's review_findings_delta key (tuned for a differently-defined metric in promotion.evaluate()) means an unrelated future edit to promotion.CRITERIA silently changes this module's noninferior gate.

first_pass_rate is specified as 'owned roots with pipeline.lineage_fix_rounds in (0, None) and no fix-round children' with no requirement that the root has actually resolved (merged_into set, reached first_green, or failed). Unlike downstream_accepted_rate (which conservatively counts an unresolved task as 'not yet accepted'), an in-flight execute task with no fix rounds yet defaults to counting as a first-pass success. Existing scorecard.efficiency() treats an undefined first_pass as None until pipeline.first_green_at is stamped (scorecard.py:1037) specifically to avoid this. Because class_evidence gates noninferior promotion partly on first_pass_delta (>= -0.02), a candidate model whose tasks are simply younger/still-running will look artificially better than a baseline with a longer-settled task mix, biasing exactly the promotion decision this module exists to inform.
